messages:
kevin (api): quick pulse-check: internal routing model discussion - should we centralize route decisions in a single gateway, or push routing down to each service (service-front proxy)?
alex (platform): leaning service-front proxies. teams can iterate faster and do per-service canaries without central deploy.
rachel (product): console perspective: we can't flood customers with thousands of tiny routes. need aggregated / rollup views and easy search.
tomo (devex): agree with alex on delegation for latency, also makes localized header enrichment simpler. but we must define a canonical route identifier so telemetry ties back to product metrics.
kevin (api): proposing hybrid: runtime routing happens at service-front proxies, but control-plane owns canonical route catalog + rollout config and global policy snapshots.
leo (sre): reliability note: single gateway amplifies blast radius. prefer distributed proxies with a small central enforcement layer for billing caps.
tomo (devex): telemetry contract idea: each runtime proxy MUST emit a label triple: org/service/route_key and a rollout_tag (primary|canary|shadow). console will map those into grouped dashboards.
kevin (api): sample header to standardize: ```
X-RW-Route: org:service:route_key
X-RW-Rollout: primary|canary|shadow
```
deploy-bot: schema-update: X-RW-Route added to header whitelist (proto v3).
alex (platform): quotas decision:
- Sync-check (central call per request): consistent but latency + central load
- Local token-bucket with control-plane sync: scalable but eventual consistency
Which do we pick?
rachel (product): prefer local token-buckets if the console shows sync state and "last-sync"/"stale" indicators. customers tolerate short slippage if it's visible.
leo (sre): add a backstop: central enforcer that only triggers on high-cost or billing-bound events. keeps local flow cheap but safe for billing.
tomo (devex): rollout UX requirements: 1) set canary percent per route, 2) automatic fallback on error_pct or latency regression, 3) single-click rollback in console. Delegated proxies must accept rollout updates via config stream.
kevin (api): implementation sketch:
1) Control plane publishes route catalog (proto) + rollout blobs
2) Proxies subscribe via streaming API (gRPC) and apply rules locally
3) Proxies emit canonical headers and per-request metrics to tracing backend
4) Console shows aggregated (service-level) and exploded (route-level) views with search and canary slider

alex (platform): we also need a route-id canonicalization spec (no slashes in keys, stable across deploys). I'll draft that.
rachel (product): retention question: how long do we keep per-route telemetry? incl. metrics and detailed traces?
leo (sre): propose metrics/agg: 365d; detailed traces: 90d; raw request logs: 30d. gate longer retention to paid tiers.
tomo (devex): proto vs JSON for control-plane payloads? protos are stricter and easier for SDKs, JSON easier for ad-hoc edits in UI.
kevin (api): suggestion: use proto on the wire and provide JSON editor in console that the control-plane compiles & validates into proto.
alex (platform): agree. security note: control-plane should sign rollout blobs so proxies validate authenticity (JWT or mTLS).
leo (sre): add health-check endpoints per-proxy and a central "rollout observed rate" metric to detect stuck updates.
kevin (api): action items: kevin -> route-id spec PR; alex -> token-bucket sync design doc; tomo -> console mock (grouped view + canary control); leo -> SLOs & retention numbers.
rachel (product): can we poll quickly? default decision = delegated service-front proxies + unified control-plane for catalog/telemetry/backstop. please react by EOD.
tomo (devex): :thumbsup:
leo (sre): :thumbsup:
kevin (api): :thumbsup: I'll open the PR and link here.
deploy-bot: control-plane canary started (cp-canary-2026-07).
